seal_overflow records only the MESH clamp (MAX_SEAL_RADIUS=2); the COLLIDER clamp (MAX_BODY_RADIUS=6) is the one that can strand a walker and it records nothing. A mesh overflow cannot cause a stall - colliders seal unclamped 45 lines below the comment that says otherwise.

em_built.json's cell grid is stamped in _write_built (endless_museum.gd:3453) BEFORE the deferred dressing pass (queued :3319) erases bench and prop cells, and _run_dress_item (:7050) re-flushes the file afterwards with fresh mtime and cards but the same stale grid -- so a replay segment's grid is the undressed shell. Dressing is subtractive, so a cut in the shell is real (FAIL sound) but a whole shell earns no PASS.

endless_museum.gd clamps a body's footprint TWICE - meshes to MAX_SEAL_RADIUS 2, colliders to MAX_BODY_RADIUS 6 - and only the mesh half recorded its overflow. The collider half is the only one that can strand a walker (there is no decorative collider), so the seal_overflow:0 printed beside three failed gate F runs was a fact about what the counter counted, not about the corridor. Both halves now record through one static classifier with a 'by' tag, tested by 8 synthetic cases of which 4 must stay SILENT.
